# Review pack: Musa

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/musa.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review. English only; Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quranic text in the repo (Tanzil Uthmani) only; no hadith, no tafsir, no sira, no Biblical material in this phase. Hadith to add later: reports on the journey with the servant (18:60-82), on the Samiri, on the manner of the plagues and the sea, and on the death and burial of Musa. Names and details found only in later tradition are kept in unknowns_md and uncertainties_en. Quotation marks surround only speech recorded in the cited ayat (English renderings are drafts for translator and scholar review). The Quran tells Musa's account in many surahs; each chapter keeps the surahs apart and does not treat surah order as chronology. The cow of Banu Isra'il (2:67-73) is not covered in this draft. Nothing here is reviewed or published.

## Story-level uncertainties

- The identity and name of Fir'awn are not given in the Quran; none is used here.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the mother, sister and wife of Musa, of the father of the women of Madyan, of the servant, of Musa's young man, of the men of 5:23 and of the believing man of Fir'awn's family. None is used in the chapters.
- Surah order is not chronology. The Quran tells the call, the signs, the magicians and the sea in more than one place; the chapters keep them separate and do not merge them.
- The speaker of 28:19 is not marked in the text; interpreters differ.
- The meanings of the phrase kill yourselves in 2:54, qiblah in 10:87, misran in 2:61, the greatest sign, the quake in 7:155 and the thunderbolt in 2:55 are read in more than one way; the draft renderings are for review.
- The Musa of 18:60-82 is read as the Musa of the other ayat by common reading, but this is not stated in the ayat.
- The inventory refs of this subject were widened to include 2:63, 2:93, 4:154, 7:171, 19:51-53 and 44:23-31 (an additive inventory migration; see the story drafts workflow document). The passage on the mountain raised over a people (2:63, 2:93, 4:154, 7:171) does not name Musa in its ayat; a scholar should confirm that it belongs under this subject.
- Hadith to add later: reports on the staff, the Samiri, the plagues, the servant, the death of Musa and the meetings of prophets, each with its grading.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The decree and the river  (`#birth-and-the-river`)

Cited ayat: 28:3-7, 20:37-39

> **28:3** نَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكَ مِن نَّبَإِ مُوسَىٰ وَفِرْعَوْنَ بِٱلْحَقِّ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
>
> **28:4** إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَهَا شِيَعًا يَسْتَضْعِفُ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَيَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
>
> **28:5** وَنُرِيدُ أَن نَّمُنَّ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتُضْعِفُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَنَجْعَلَهُمْ أَئِمَّةً وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
>
> **28:6** وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَنُرِىَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَحْذَرُونَ
>
> **28:7** وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

> **20:37** وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰٓ
>
> **20:38** إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ
>
> **20:39** أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ

### Claims

**c1** (28:3): God recites the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth, for a people who believe.

**c2** (28:4): Fir'awn exalted himself in the land, made its people into factions, oppressed one group of them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive; he was among the corrupters.

**c3** (28:5-6): God says He wished to favour those who were oppressed in the land, make them leaders and inheritors, establish them in the land, and show Fir'awn, Haman and their soldiers what they feared from them.

**c4** (28:7): God inspired the mother of Musa and told her “Nurse him; and when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear or grieve; we will return him to you and make him one of the messengers.”

**c5** (20:37-39): In another passage, God reminds Musa that He had favoured him another time, when He inspired his mother what was inspired: to put him in the chest and put it into the river, so that the river would cast it up on the bank where an enemy of God and of Musa would take him.

**c6** (20:39): God says He cast love from Himself upon Musa, so that he would be brought up under His eye.

### One-minute summary

The account begins with Fir'awn's oppression of one group in his land [c2] and God's wish to favour the oppressed [c3]. God inspired the mother of Musa to nurse him and, when she feared, to cast him into the river, with a promise to return him and make him a messenger [c4]. Another passage tells the same favour with the chest [c5].

### Complete story

God says He recites the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth for a people who believe [c1]. Fir'awn exalted himself in the land and divided its people into factions, oppressing one group by slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive [c2]. God says He wished to favour the oppressed, make them leaders and inheritors, and show Fir'awn, Haman and their soldiers what they feared [c3].

God inspired Musa's mother: nurse him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river; do not fear or grieve; He would return him to her and make him one of the messengers [c4]. Another passage recalls this as a further favour: the child was to be put in a chest and the chest in the river, which would cast it on the bank, where an enemy of God and of Musa would take him [c5]. God cast love from Himself upon Musa so that he would be brought up under His eye [c6].

### Deep study

One passage frames the decree with Fir'awn's policy and God's wish to favour the oppressed [c2][c3], then gives the instruction to the mother with a promise [c4]. Another gives the instruction as a favour recalled to Musa himself and adds the chest and the bank [c5], and the love cast upon him [c6]. Both agree on the river [c4][c5]. Haman is already named as one of the people God wished to show what they feared [c3].

### Kids mode

Fir'awn oppressed one group of people in his land [c2]. God told the mother of Musa to nurse her baby, and when she was afraid, to put him in the river [c4]. God promised to give him back to her and to make him one of His messengers [c4]. God put love for Musa in the hearts of those who found him [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the passage presents a promise made before the danger was over, and a mother asked to act on it [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the name of Musa's mother, the name of the river (the ayat say yamm, 'the river' or 'the sea'), the date, the number of years of the oppression, and the name or dynasty of Fir'awn. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the personal names of Musa's mother and sister, the name of the river, and any dates. The sentence at 28:6 says Haman; the Quran gives no further detail on his office.

## 2. Found, returned and raised  (`#in-the-household-of-firawn`)

Cited ayat: 28:8-13, 20:40, 26:18

> **28:8** فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ
>
> **28:9** وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
>
> **28:10** وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِى بِهِۦ لَوْلَآ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **28:11** وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
>
> **28:12** وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ
>
> **28:13** فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

> **20:40** إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُۥ فَرَجَعْنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يَٰمُوسَىٰ

> **26:18** قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (28:8): The family of Fir'awn picked him up so that he would become to them an enemy and a grief; God says Fir'awn, Haman and their soldiers were sinners.

**c2** (28:9): The wife of Fir'awn said “A joy of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son”, and they did not perceive.

**c3** (28:10): The heart of Musa's mother became empty; she was about to disclose it had God not strengthened her heart so that she would be among the believers.

**c4** (28:11): She told his sister to follow him; the sister watched him from a distance while they did not perceive.

**c5** (28:12): God had forbidden wet-nurses to him beforehand; the sister said “Shall I direct you to a household who will take care of him for you and be sincere to him?”

**c6** (28:13, 20:40): God returned him to his mother so that her eye would be cooled and she would not grieve, and so that she would know that God's promise is true.

**c7** (26:18): Later, Fir'awn said to Musa “Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed among us for years of your life?”

### One-minute summary

The family of Fir'awn picked him up [c1], and Fir'awn's wife said not to kill him [c2]. His mother's heart was emptied and God strengthened it [c3]. His sister followed him [c4], asked whether she could direct them to a household to nurse him [c5], and God returned him to his mother [c6]. Fir'awn later reminded Musa that he had been raised among them [c7].

### Complete story

The family of Fir'awn picked up the child so that he would become to them an enemy and a grief [c1]. The wife of Fir'awn said he was a joy of the eye for her and for Fir'awn, that they should not kill him, and that perhaps he would benefit them or be adopted as a son; they did not perceive [c2]. The heart of Musa's mother became empty, and she would nearly have disclosed him had God not strengthened her heart [c3]. She told his sister to follow him, and the sister watched from a distance while they did not perceive [c4]. God had forbidden wet-nurses to the child beforehand, and the sister said she could direct them to a household who would take care of him and be sincere to him [c5]. God returned him to his mother so that her eye would be cooled, she would not grieve, and she would know that God's promise is true [c6]. Another passage records Fir'awn later reminding Musa that he had been raised among them as a child and had stayed for years of his life [c7].

### Deep study

Both passages end the return with the mother's eye cooled and no more grief [c6]. Only one gives the words of the sister and of the wife [c2][c5]. God says the family picked him up so that he would become to them an enemy [c1], and the next sentence gives the wife's words about a joy of the eye [c2]; the text records both without reconciling them.

### Kids mode

Fir'awn's family found the baby [c1]. Fir'awn's wife said not to kill him, since he might be a benefit to them [c2]. Musa's sister watched from far away and asked whether she could find someone to care for him [c4][c5]. So God gave Musa back to his mother, so that she would not grieve [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the account shows the mother's fear and God's strengthening of her heart [c3], and a promise kept [c6]. It also records a good word from an unexpected person in the palace of an unjust ruler [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the names of the wife of Fir'awn (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text), of Musa's sister, and of the nursing household; the length of time; where in Fir'awn's household he lived (the ayat do not describe a building; this draft does not say palace). Whether the ‘years’ in 26:18 refers to this period or a longer one is not stated.

## 3. The killing and the flight  (`#the-killing-and-the-flight`)

Cited ayat: 28:14-21, 26:19-21, 20:40

> **28:14** وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَٱسْتَوَىٰٓ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
>
> **28:15** وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ
>
> **28:16** قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى فَٱغْفِرْ لِى فَغَفَرَ لَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
>
> **28:17** قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ
>
> **28:18** فَأَصْبَحَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَنصَرَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُۥ قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِىٌّ مُّبِينٌ
>
> **28:19** فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِى كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۢا بِٱلْأَمْسِ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ
>
> **28:20** وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَٱخْرُجْ إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
>
> **28:21** فَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ قَالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

> **26:19** وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
>
> **26:20** قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
>
> **26:21** فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُكْمًا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

> **20:40** إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُۥ فَرَجَعْنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يَٰمُوسَىٰ

### Claims

**c1** (28:14): When he reached his full strength and was established, God gave him judgement and knowledge.

**c2** (28:15): He entered the city at a time of heedlessness of its people and found a pair of men fighting, one from his party and one from his enemy; the one from his party asked him for help against the one from his enemy; Musa struck him and ended his life.

**c3** (28:15): Musa said “This is of the work of Satan; he is a manifest misleading enemy.”

**c4** (28:16-17): He said “My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me”, and God forgave him; and he said “My Lord, for the favour You have shown me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals.”

**c5** (28:18): In the morning he was in the city fearful and watching; the one who had asked for his help the day before cried out to him again, and Musa said to him “You are clearly a deviant.”

**c6** (28:19): When he wished to seize the one who was an enemy to both of them, a speaker said “Musa, do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be among the reformers.”

**c7** (28:20): A man came running from the far end of the city and said “Musa, the chiefs are conspiring about you to kill you, so leave; I am to you one of the sincere advisers.”

**c8** (28:21): He left fearful and watching, and said “My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.”

**c9** (26:19-21): Musa was later told “You did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful”; he replied “I did it then while I was among those who erred; I fled from you when I feared you; then my Lord gave me judgement and made me one of the messengers.”

**c10** (20:40): God reminds Musa that he killed a person and God delivered him from distress and tried him with trials.

### One-minute summary

Musa was given judgement and knowledge [c1]. In the city he struck a man who died [c2], called it the work of Satan, and asked forgiveness [c3][c4]. Next morning he was warned that the chiefs were conspiring to kill him [c7], and he left, asking to be saved from the wrongdoing people [c8].

### Complete story

When Musa reached his full strength, God gave him judgement and knowledge [c1]. He entered the city when its people were heedless and found a pair of men fighting; the one from his party asked for his help against his enemy, Musa struck the other, and ended his life [c2]. He said it was of the work of Satan, a manifest misleading enemy [c3], and asked his Lord to forgive him, which God did; he said he would never be a supporter of the criminals [c4].

In the morning he was fearful and watching; the man who had asked for his help the day before cried out again, and Musa called him a clear deviant [c5]. As Musa wished to seize the one who was an enemy to both, a speaker said he wanted to be a tyrant and not a reformer, asking if he meant to kill as he had killed the day before [c6]. A man came running from the far end of the city with a warning that the chiefs were conspiring to kill him, and told him to leave [c7]. Musa left, fearful and watching, and asked to be saved from the wrongdoing people [c8].

Musa was later told that he had done his deed and was of the ungrateful, and he answered that he did it when he erred, fled from fear, and that his Lord then gave him judgement and made him a messenger [c9]. Another passage recalls that God delivered him from distress and tried him with trials [c10].

### Deep study

The killing and the fear are recorded in more than one passage [c2][c9][c10]. One gives the sequence of the days [c2][c5], the prayer for forgiveness and the forgiveness [c4], and the running man [c7]. Musa's own account of it is brief and ties the flight to fear [c9]. The first act is called the work of Satan [c3], and Musa calls himself one who wronged himself [c4].

### Kids mode

One day in the city Musa tried to help a man, and a fight ended in a man's death [c2]. Musa said he had wronged himself and asked God to forgive him, and God forgave him [c4]. A man ran to warn him that the chiefs wanted to harm him, and Musa left the city and asked God to save him [c7][c8].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the account records a prophet admitting a wrong, asking for forgiveness, and being forgiven [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: which of the pair men is meant by ‘from his party’ and ‘from his enemy’ beyond those words, the name of the city, who spoke in 28:19 (interpreters differ), how Musa struck the man, the name of the man who warned him (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text), and the length of the interval between the events. Another passage 26:20 uses a word that interpreters render in different ways (‘erred’, ‘was unaware’); this draft gives one rendering for review.

## 4. Madyan  (`#madyan`)

Cited ayat: 28:22-28, 20:40

> **28:22** وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِى سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
>
> **28:23** وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ
>
> **28:24** فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ
>
> **28:25** فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا تَمْشِى عَلَى ٱسْتِحْيَآءٍ قَالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِى يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ مَا سَقَيْتَ لَنَا فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
>
> **28:26** قَالَتْ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسْتَـْٔجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ ٱسْتَـْٔجَرْتَ ٱلْقَوِىُّ ٱلْأَمِينُ
>
> **28:27** قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُنكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ٱبْنَتَىَّ هَٰتَيْنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأْجُرَنِى ثَمَٰنِىَ حِجَجٍ فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِنْ عِندِكَ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
>
> **28:28** قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكَ أَيَّمَا ٱلْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلَا عُدْوَٰنَ عَلَىَّ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ

> **20:40** إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُۥ فَرَجَعْنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يَٰمُوسَىٰ

### Claims

**c1** (28:22): As he turned toward Madyan he said “Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.”

**c2** (28:23): At the water of Madyan he found a group of people watering and, apart from them, a pair of women holding back; he asked “What is your affair?” and they said “We cannot water until the shepherds leave, and our father is an old man.”

**c3** (28:24): He watered for them, withdrew to the shade, and said “My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.”

**c4** (28:25): One of the pair came to him walking shyly and said “My father invites you to pay you the reward for watering for us”; when he came to the father and told him his story, the father said “Do not fear; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.”

**c5** (28:26): One of the pair said “Father, hire him; the best you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.”

**c6** (28:27): The father said he wished to marry one of his daughters here to him on condition that he serve him for eight years, and that if he completed ten it would be from him; he did not wish to burden him, and Musa would find him, if God willed, among the righteous.

**c7** (28:28): Musa said “That is between me and you; whichever of the pair terms I complete, there is no injustice to me; and God is a witness over what we say.”

**c8** (20:40): Another passage says he stayed for years among the people of Madyan and then came at a decreed time.

### One-minute summary

Musa turned toward Madyan [c1], helped a pair of women at the water [c2][c3], was invited by their father [c4], and was offered a marriage in return for service for eight years, with ten as a favour [c6]. He accepted the terms [c7]. Another passage says he stayed years among the people of Madyan [c8].

### Complete story

As Musa turned toward Madyan he said he hoped his Lord would guide him to the right way [c1]. At the water he found people watering and a pair of women holding back; they told him they could not water until the shepherds left and that their father was an old man [c2]. He watered for them, withdrew to the shade, and said he was in need of whatever good God would send to him [c3]. One of them came shyly to invite him from her father to be paid for the watering; the father, hearing his story, told him not to fear for he had escaped the wrongdoing people [c4]. One said her father should hire him as the strong and trustworthy [c5].

The father offered to marry him to one of his daughters here in return for eight years of service, with ten as a favour from Musa if he completed them [c6]. Musa agreed to the terms and made God a witness [c7]. Another passage says Musa stayed for years among the people of Madyan and then came at a decreed time [c8].

### Deep study

The passage gives the details of an ordinary agreement: the work, the term and the marriage [c6][c7]. The terms are a choice of lengths, with the longer a favour [c6], and Musa's reply refers to both lengths [c7]. The prayer in the shade is the only speech of Musa to God recorded between the flight and the fire in this passage [c3].

### Kids mode

Musa came to the water of Madyan and saw a pair of women who could not get water for their sheep [c2]. He helped them [c2][c3]. Later their father offered him a marriage if he served for years, and Musa agreed [c6][c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Musa helps without being asked and then asks God for good [c3]. The father's offer is made with a plain statement of terms [c6], and the daughter describes a good worker as strong and trustworthy [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the name of the father and of his daughters; whether the father was a prophet (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: a name linking him to Shu'ayb, whom the Quran elsewhere sends to Madyan, but the ayat here do not make that link); the location of Madyan; which of the pair terms Musa completed (the ayat say only that he completed the term, 28:29); and the name of the daughter he married.

## 5. The call at the mountain  (`#the-call`)

Cited ayat: 28:29-30, 20:9-16, 27:7-9, 79:15-16, 19:51-52

> **28:29** فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلْأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهْلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارًا قَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ
>
> **28:30** فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ مِن شَٰطِئِ ٱلْوَادِ ٱلْأَيْمَنِ فِى ٱلْبُقْعَةِ ٱلْمُبَٰرَكَةِ مِنَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ أَن يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

> **20:9** وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰٓ
>
> **20:10** إِذْ رَءَا نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى
>
> **20:11** فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ
>
> **20:12** إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
>
> **20:13** وَأَنَا ٱخْتَرْتُكَ فَٱسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَىٰٓ
>
> **20:14** إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدْنِى وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ
>
> **20:15** إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا تَسْعَىٰ

> **27:7** إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَهْلِهِۦٓ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا سَـَٔاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ

>
> **79:16** إِذْ نَادَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى

> **19:51** وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مُخْلَصًا وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَّبِيًّا
>
> **19:52** وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنِ وَقَرَّبْنَٰهُ نَجِيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (28:29, 20:9-10, 27:7): When Musa had completed the term and set out with his family, he perceived a fire on the side of the mountain (at-Tur) and said to his family “Stay here; I have perceived a fire; perhaps I will bring you news from it, or a burning brand from the fire so that you may warm yourselves.”

**c2** (28:30): When he came to it he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: “Musa, I am God, the Lord of the worlds.”

**c3** (20:11-12): In another passage, he was called “Musa, I am your Lord, so take off your sandals; you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.”

**c4** (20:13-14): He was told “I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed; I am God, there is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.”

**c5** (20:15-16): He was told that the Hour is coming, which God almost keeps hidden, so that every soul is recompensed for its striving, and not to let the one who does not believe in it and follows his desire turn him from it.

**c6** (27:8-9): In another passage, the call says “Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it, and glory be to God, Lord of the worlds. Musa, it is I, God, the Almighty, the Wise.”

**c7** (79:15-16): Another passage asks whether the account of Musa has reached the listener, when his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa.

**c8** (19:51-52): A further passage says of Musa that he was chosen (mukhlas), a messenger and a prophet; that God called him from the right side of the mountain (at-Tur) and brought him near in private converse.

### One-minute summary

On the way with his family Musa saw a fire and went to bring news or a brand from it [c1]. He was called from the valley, “I am God, the Lord of the worlds” [c2], told to take off his sandals [c3], told that he was chosen, to worship God and establish prayer [c4], and told of the coming Hour [c5]. Other passages say that his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa [c7], and that he was chosen, a messenger and a prophet, brought near in private converse [c8].

### Complete story

Musa, having completed the term and set out with his family, perceived a fire on the side of the mountain and told his family to stay while he went to bring news from it or a burning brand [c1]. As he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: “Musa, I am God, the Lord of the worlds” [c2]. The call also says “I am your Lord, so take off your sandals; you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa” [c3]. He was told that he was chosen and should listen to what is revealed, that God is God, there is no god but Him, and to worship Him and establish prayer for His remembrance [c4], and that the Hour is coming [c5]. Another passage adds the call “Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it” and “Musa, it is I, God, the Almighty, the Wise” [c6].

Another passage asks whether the account of Musa has reached the listener, when his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa [c7]. A further passage says he was chosen, a messenger and a prophet, that God called him from the right side of the mountain and brought him near in private converse [c8].

### Deep study

The passages agree on the fire [c1], the valley [c3] and the call by name [c2][c3][c6]. The call is described as coming from the tree [c2], and the ayat say no more about the tree. Some of what Musa was told is given in separate passages: the identity of the caller [c2][c6], the command to take off his sandals [c3], the central message of worship and prayer [c4], and the coming Hour [c5]. Other passages add to this: one opens with a question to the listener [c7], and one describes Musa as chosen, a messenger and a prophet who was brought near in private converse [c8].

### Kids mode

Musa saw a fire and went toward it to bring his family some news or a piece of it to warm them [c1]. A voice called out: “Musa, I am God, the Lord of the worlds” [c2]. God told him to take off his sandals because he was in a holy valley [c3]. God told him to worship Him and to pray [c4]. Musa was a messenger and a prophet whom God called and brought near [c8].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the message Musa received first is about worship and prayer [c4], with a reminder of the coming Hour [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the exact place or the date, what the fire was, what the tree was, which night, and the names of those with him. The ayat say his family and do not list them. The caller's voice is described only as a call. Whether whoever is in the fire names a specific being is read differently by interpreters; this draft makes no claim. The word rendered chosen in 19:51 (mukhlas) is read as mukhlis, one who is sincere, in a variant reading; the page should state which reading it follows.

## 6. The staff, the hand and Harun  (`#the-staff-the-hand-and-harun`)

Cited ayat: 20:17-36, 28:31-35, 27:10-12, 19:53

> **20:17** وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
>
> **20:18** قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ
>
> **20:19** قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
>

>
> **20:22** وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ
>
> **20:23** لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى
>

> **19:53** وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ مِن رَّحْمَتِنَآ أَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ نَبِيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (20:17-18): God asked “What is that in your right hand, Musa?” and he said “It is my staff; I lean on it, I beat down leaves with it for my sheep, and I have other uses for it.”

**c2** (20:19-21): He was told to throw it, and it became a moving snake; he was told “Take it and do not fear; we will return it to its first state.”

**c3** (28:31, 27:10): In another passage, and another passage, when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not look back; he was told to come forward and not to fear, that he was secure, and that the messengers do not fear in God's presence.

**c4** (20:22-23, 28:32, 27:12): He was told to draw his hand to his side or put it in his bosom, and it would come out white without harm, as another sign; these are a pair of proofs from his Lord to Fir'awn and his chiefs, who were a defiantly disobedient people, among nine signs.

**c5** (20:24): He was told to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed.

**c6** (20:25-36): Musa prayed “My Lord, expand my chest for me, ease my task for me, and loosen the knot from my tongue so that they understand my speech; appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun my brother; strengthen my back with him and let him share in my task, so that we may glorify You much and remember You much; You are ever seeing us.” God said “You have been given your request, Musa.”

**c7** (28:33-34): In another passage, he said “My Lord, I killed a person among them, so I fear they will kill me; my brother Harun is more fluent than I in speech, so send him with me as support to confirm me; I fear they will deny me.”

**c8** (28:35): God said “We will strengthen your arm with your brother and give you both authority so that they cannot reach you; with Our signs, both of you and those who follow you will be the victors.”

**c9** (19:53): A further passage says that out of His mercy God gave Musa his brother Harun as a prophet.

**c10** (27:11): The ayah after the reassurance in 27:10 makes an exception: except for one who did wrong and then replaced it, after evil, with good; for such, God says, He is Forgiving, Merciful.

### One-minute summary

Musa was asked about what was in his hand and answered it was his staff [c1]. It became a moving snake and then was returned to its first state [c2]; he was told not to fear [c3]. His hand came out white as another sign [c4]. He was sent to Fir'awn [c5] and prayed for ease, and for Harun to be with him [c6][c7]. God said He would strengthen his arm with his brother [c8]. Another passage says that out of His mercy God gave Musa his brother Harun as a prophet [c9].

### Complete story

God asked Musa what was in his right hand, and he said it was his staff, on which he leaned and with which he beat down leaves for his sheep, with other uses besides [c1]. He was told to throw it, and it became a moving snake; he was told to take it without fear, for it would return to its first state [c2]. In other passages he turned in flight and was told to come forward, that he was secure, and that messengers do not fear in God's presence [c3]. He was told to put his hand into his bosom, and it would come out white without harm, as another sign, among nine signs to Fir'awn and his people, who were defiantly disobedient [c4]. He was told to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed [c5].

Musa then prayed for his chest to be expanded, his task eased, the knot loosened from his tongue so that they would understand his speech, and for Harun his brother as a minister to strengthen his back and share in his task; God answered that his request was granted [c6]. Another passage gives the reason: he had killed a person among them and feared being killed, and Harun was more fluent in speech [c7]. God said He would strengthen his arm with his brother and give both authority, so that they could not be reached, and they and their followers would be the victors [c8].

Another passage adds that out of His mercy God gave Musa his brother Harun as a prophet [c9]. The ayah after the reassurance to the messengers makes an exception, for one who did wrong and then replaced it with good after evil, and says that God is Forgiving, Merciful [c10].

### Deep study

The staff and the hand are told in separate passages with different emphasis [c1][c3][c4]. One has the question about the staff and the gentle command to take the snake [c1][c2]; others have Musa's flight and the reassurance [c3]. The request for Harun is given as a prayer for ease and a helper [c6] and as a reason of the killing and fluency [c7], and God's answer speaks of authority and victory [c8]. The signs are called nine signs and proofs [c4]; the ayat in this draft do not list the nine. The ayah that follows the reassurance in 27:10 begins with an exception, and how the exception relates to what comes before it is read in more than one way [c10].

### Kids mode

God asked Musa what he held, and he said it was his staff [c1]. God told him to throw it, and it became a moving snake [c2]. Then God told him not to be afraid [c3]. God gave him another sign with his hand [c4]. Musa asked God to make his task easy and to send his brother Harun to help him, and God granted his request [c6][c8]. God also gave Musa his brother Harun as a prophet [c9].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Musa does not simply accept the task; he asks for ease, for clearer speech, and for his brother's help [c6].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in these ayat: what the nine signs are, since the plagues are listed elsewhere and are not assumed to be the nine; what the knot in Musa's tongue was, since the ayat state only the request; the age of Harun relative to Musa; and where Harun was when he was sent for. The grammar of the exception in 27:11, and whom it refers to, is discussed by interpreters; this draft states the words and draws no conclusion about Musa or anyone else.

### Claims

**c1** (20:42-44): God told Musa and his brother to go with His signs and not slacken in remembering Him, to go to Fir'awn who had transgressed, and to speak to him a gentle word, so that perhaps he would remember or fear.

**c2** (20:45-46): They said “Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us or transgress”; God said “Do not fear; I am with you both, hearing and seeing.”

**c3** (26:10-15): In another passage, God called Musa to go to the wrongdoing people, the people of Fir'awn, asking “Will they not be mindful?”; Musa said “My Lord, I fear that they will deny me, my chest is straitened and my tongue is not fluent, so send for Harun; they also have a charge against me, so I fear they will kill me”; God said “No; go both of you with Our signs; we are with you, listening.”

**c4** (20:47-48, 26:16-17): They were to say to Fir'awn “We are a pair of messengers of your Lord (the messenger of the Lord of the worlds): send the Children of Israel with us and do not torment them; we have come to you with a sign from your Lord; peace be upon the one who follows the guidance.”

**c5** (26:18-21): Fir'awn said “Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed among us for years of your life? And you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful.” Musa said that he had done it then while he erred, fled when he feared, and was then given judgement and made one of the messengers.

**c6** (26:22): Musa said “That is a favour you hold over me: that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.” (Interpreters read this sentence as a statement or as a question.)

**c7** (20:49-52): Fir'awn asked “Who is your Lord, Musa?” and Musa said “Our Lord is He who gave everything its form and then guided.” Fir'awn asked about the earlier generations and Musa said their knowledge is with his Lord in a record; his Lord neither errs nor forgets.

**c8** (26:23-28): In another passage, Fir'awn asked “And what is the Lord of the worlds?” Musa answered “The Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if you are convinced”, then “Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers”, then “The Lord of the east and the west and what is between them, if you use reason.”

**c9** (26:25-27): Fir'awn said to those around him “Do you not hear?” and said “Your messenger who was sent to you is surely mad.”

**c10** (26:29-31): Fir'awn said “If you take a god other than me, I will make you one of the imprisoned.” Musa said “Even if I bring you something clear?” Fir'awn said “Bring it, if you are of the truthful.”

**c11** (79:17-19): Another passage says Musa was told to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed, and to say “Would you be purified, and shall I guide you to your Lord so that you fear?”

### One-minute summary

Musa and Harun were sent to Fir'awn with a gentle word [c1], having voiced their fear and been told God was with them [c2][c3]. Their message was to send the Children of Israel with them [c4]. Fir'awn reminded Musa of the years in his household [c5], asked who the Lord is [c7][c8], called Musa mad [c9] and threatened prison [c10]. Another passage adds the question whether Fir'awn would be purified [c11].

### Complete story

God told Musa and his brother to go to Fir'awn with His signs, not to slacken in remembering Him, and to speak a gentle word so that perhaps Fir'awn would remember or fear [c1]. They said they feared he would hasten against them or transgress, and God said He was with them, hearing and seeing [c2]. In another passage Musa voiced fear of being denied, his tongue not being fluent, and a charge against him, and asked that Harun be sent for; God said to go with His signs and that He was listening [c3].

The message was that they were messengers and that Fir'awn should send the Children of Israel with them and not torment them, with peace on the one who follows the guidance [c4]. Fir'awn answered by recalling the years Musa stayed with them and his deed, and Musa replied that he had done it while he erred, fled from fear, and was given judgement and made a messenger [c5]. Musa said the favour Fir'awn held over him was that he had enslaved the Children of Israel [c6].

Fir'awn asked who the Lord is; in another passage Musa answered that He gave everything its form and then guided, and that the knowledge of earlier generations is with his Lord in a record [c7]. In another passage he answered with the Lord of the heavens and the earth, of the forefathers, and of the east and the west [c8]. Fir'awn asked those around if they heard and called Musa mad [c9], then threatened to imprison him if he took a god other than Fir'awn; Musa asked if he would do so even if he brought something clear [c10]. Another passage records the instruction to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed, and to ask whether he would be purified and offer to guide him to his Lord so that he would fear [c11].

### Deep study

The meeting is told in more than one passage, each keeping a part of the exchange [c1][c3][c8]. One has the instruction to speak gently and God's assurance [c1][c2]. Another has Musa's fears [c3], Fir'awn's reminder of his upbringing and deed [c5][c6], and the series of questions [c8]. Fir'awn's statements about Musa, that he is mad [c9] and that he would imprison him [c10], are in one passage only. The question whether Fir'awn would be purified, with the offer of guidance, is in one passage only [c11].

### Kids mode

God told Musa and Harun to speak to Fir'awn kindly [c1]. They were a little afraid, and God told them He was with them, hearing and seeing [c1][c2]. They asked Fir'awn to let the Children of Israel go with them [c4]. Fir'awn asked who their Lord was, and Musa said He is the one who gave everything its shape and then guided it [c7]. God also told Musa to ask Fir'awn whether he would be purified, and to offer to guide him to his Lord [c11].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the instruction to a messenger facing a tyrant is to speak a gentle word first [c1], and the assurance given to the frightened is that God is hearing and seeing [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: where the meeting took place, how many times it happened, which passage describes the first meeting, and the personal name or period of this Fir'awn. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification with a named ruler of Egypt. The Arabic wording of 20:50, rendered here gave everything its form, has more than one possible rendering for scholarly review. How the instruction in 79:17-19 relates to the other passages of this chapter is not stated.

### Claims

**c1** (7:103-105): God sent Musa with His signs to Fir'awn and his chiefs; Musa said “Fir'awn, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, bound to say nothing about God but the truth; I have come to you with clear proof from your Lord, so send the Children of Israel with me.”

**c2** (7:106-108, 26:32-33): Fir'awn said “If you have come with a sign, bring it, if you are of the truthful.” Musa threw his staff and it was a clear serpent; he drew out his hand and it was white to the onlookers.

**c3** (7:109-112, 26:34-37): The chiefs said “This is a learned magician who wants to drive you out of your land”, and Fir'awn asked what they advise; they said to delay him and his brother and send gatherers into the cities to bring every learned magician.

**c4** (10:75-77): God sent Musa and Harun to Fir'awn and his chiefs; they were arrogant and a criminal people; when the truth came, they said “This is clear magic”, and Musa said “Do you say this of the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic? The magicians do not succeed.”

**c5** (10:78): They said “Have you come to turn us from what we found our fathers following, so that greatness in the land may be yours? We are not believers in both of you.”

**c6** (23:45-48): They said “Shall we believe a pair of humans like ourselves, whose people are servants to us?”, denied them, and were among the destroyed.

**c7** (28:36-37): They said “This is nothing but forged magic, and we never heard of this among our earlier forefathers”; Musa said “My Lord knows best who comes with guidance from Him and who will have the final home; the wrongdoers do not succeed.”

**c8** (28:38): Fir'awn said “O chiefs, I do not know of any god for you other than me; so kindle for me, Haman, a fire upon clay and build me a tower so that I may look at the God of Musa; I think he is one of the liars.”

**c9** (40:23-25): In another passage, Musa was sent with signs and clear authority to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, who said “a magician, a liar”; when he brought the truth they said to kill the sons of those who believed with him and keep their women alive.

**c10** (40:26-27): Fir'awn said “Let me kill Musa and let him call upon his Lord; I fear that he will change your religion or cause corruption to appear in the land.” Musa said “I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account.”

**c11** (40:28): A believing man from the family of Fir'awn, who was concealing his faith, asked “Would you kill a man because he says ‘My Lord is God’, when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is a liar, his lie is upon him; if he is truthful, some of what he promises will strike you.”

**c12** (79:20-26): Another passage says that Musa showed him the greatest sign, and he denied and disobeyed, then turned away striving, gathered and called out, and said “I am your lord, the most high”; God seized him with the punishment (nakal) of the last and the first; in that is a lesson for whoever fears.

### One-minute summary

Musa brought clear proof and asked Fir'awn to send the Children of Israel with him [c1]. He showed the staff and the hand [c2]. The chiefs called it magic and proposed gathering magicians [c3][c4]. Fir'awn claimed a position no other god was known to the chiefs [c8] and spoke of killing Musa [c10]; a believer from his family spoke against it [c11]. Another passage says that he denied the greatest sign, claimed to be the most high lord, and was seized by God [c12].

### Complete story

Musa told Fir'awn that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, bound to say only the truth, with clear proof, and asked him to send the Children of Israel with him [c1]. Fir'awn said to bring a sign if he was truthful; Musa threw his staff and it was a clear serpent, and his hand came out white to the onlookers [c2]. The chiefs said he was a learned magician who wanted to drive them out of the land, and advised gathering every learned magician [c3].

Another passage says that when the truth came they called it clear magic, and Musa asked how they could call it magic when magicians do not succeed [c4]; they replied that he came to turn them from their fathers' way and to gain greatness in the land [c5]. Another passage records them saying they would not believe a pair of humans like themselves whose people served them [c6]. Another passage records the answer ‘forged magic’ and Musa's reply that his Lord knows best who brings guidance [c7], and Fir'awn's saying that he knew no god for the chiefs but himself and his order to Haman to build a tower [c8]. Another passage names Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, who said ‘a magician, a liar’, and ordered the killing of the sons of the believers [c9]. Fir'awn said he wished to kill Musa, fearing for their religion; Musa sought refuge in his Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account [c10]. A believing man from Fir'awn's family concealing his faith asked whether they would kill a man for saying ‘My Lord is God’ [c11].

Another passage says Musa showed him the greatest sign, and he denied and disobeyed, turned away striving, gathered and called out that he was their lord, the most high; God seized him with the punishment of the last and the first, and in that is a lesson for whoever fears [c12].

### Deep study

The passages share one pattern: a sign is shown and called magic [c2][c4][c7][c9], those in authority respond with fear of loss of land and ancestral ways [c3][c5][c10], and Fir'awn makes a claim for himself [c8]. One passage adds a figure not seen elsewhere in this draft, a believing man in Fir'awn's own family [c11]. The passage that ends with a lesson for whoever fears [c12] is the only one in this chapter that tells how Fir'awn was seized.

### Kids mode

Musa showed Fir'awn the signs God gave him [c2]. Fir'awn and his chiefs said it was magic [c4][c7]. Fir'awn said he knew of no god for them but himself [c8]. One man in Fir'awn's family secretly believed, and he asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God [c11]. Fir'awn denied the greatest sign and God seized him, and there is a lesson in that for whoever fears [c12].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the account notes that clear signs can be explained away by those who fear to lose position [c3][c5], and that a single voice from inside such a court spoke in defence of what was right [c11].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the time and place of each meeting with the court, how many conversations there were, the identity and name of the believing man (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text), and who Qarun and Haman were beyond what is said in the ayat. The phrase the punishment of the last and the first in 79:25 is read in more than one way by interpreters (for example the Hereafter and this world, or his last and his first saying); this draft states the words and does not choose.

### Claims

**c1** (20:57-59): In another passage, Fir'awn said “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, Musa? We will bring you magic like it; so set an appointment between us and you, which neither we nor you shall fail, at a place midway.” Musa said “Your appointment is the day of the festival, and let the people be gathered at forenoon.”

**c2** (20:60-61): Fir'awn turned away, gathered his plan, then came; Musa said to them “Woe to you, do not invent a lie against God, lest He destroy you with a punishment; whoever invents has failed.”

**c3** (26:38-40): The magicians were gathered for the appointed time of a known day, and the people were asked whether they would gather, so that they might follow the magicians if they were the victors.

**c4** (26:41-42, 7:113-114): The magicians asked Fir'awn whether they would have a reward if they were the victors; he said “Yes, and you will then be among those brought near.”

**c5** (7:115-116, 20:65-66): They said “Musa, either you throw, or we will be the ones to throw”; he said “Throw.” when they threw, they bewitched the people and terrified them and brought great magic.

**c6** (20:66-69): Their ropes and staffs seemed to Musa, from their magic, to be moving, and Musa felt fear within himself; God said “Do not fear; you are the uppermost. Throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made; what they have made is only the trick of a magician, and the magician does not succeed wherever he comes.”

**c7** (26:45, 7:117-119): Musa threw his staff and it swallowed what they fabricated; the truth was established and what they were doing was made void, and they were defeated there and turned back humbled.

**c8** (10:79-82): In another passage, Musa said to the magicians “Throw what you will throw”, and after they threw, “What you have brought is magic; God will make it vain; God does not set right the work of the corrupters; and God establishes the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it.”

**c9** (26:46-48, 7:120-122, 20:70): The magicians were cast down in prostration, and said “We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun” (another passage has “the Lord of Harun and Musa”).

**c10** (26:49, 7:123-124, 20:71): Fir'awn said “You believed him before I gave you permission? He is your chief who taught you magic. I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides and I will crucify you all.” (another passage says on the trunks of palm trees.)

**c11** (26:50-51, 7:125-126): They said “No harm; to our Lord we will return; we hope that our Lord will forgive us our faults because we were the first of the believers”, and “You take revenge on us only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour patience upon us and take us in death as Muslims.”

**c12** (20:72-73): In another passage, they said “We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that came to us and over Him who created us; so decree whatever you decree; you only decree for this worldly life. We have believed in our Lord so that He may forgive us our faults and the magic to which you compelled us; God is better and more lasting.”

**c13** (20:62-64): In another passage, they disputed their affair among themselves and kept their private talk secret; they said “These are a pair of magicians who want to drive you out of your land by their magic and do away with your best way. So gather your plan, then come in a line; whoever has the upper hand today has succeeded.”

**c14** (26:43-44): In another passage, Musa said to them “Throw what you are going to throw”; they threw their ropes and staffs and said “By the might of Fir'awn, we are the victors.”

### One-minute summary

A day was set for Musa and the magicians [c1][c3]. They disputed among themselves and spoke of a pair of magicians who wanted to drive them out [c13]. The magicians threw first [c5], after Musa told them to throw what they were going to throw, and they spoke of the might of Fir'awn [c14] and it seemed to Musa that their ropes moved [c6]. His staff swallowed what they had made [c7]. The magicians fell down in prostration and said they believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun [c9]. Fir'awn threatened them [c10], and they answered with patience and hope for forgiveness [c11][c12].

### Complete story

Fir'awn proposed an appointment between his magicians and Musa, and Musa set the day of the festival, with the people gathered at forenoon [c1]. Fir'awn gathered his plan and came; Musa warned them not to invent a lie against God [c2]. They disputed among themselves, kept their talk secret, and said that this was a pair of magicians who wanted to drive them out of their land and do away with their best way, and told one another to gather their plan and come in a line, for whoever had the upper hand that day had succeeded [c13]. The people were asked to gather in case the magicians won [c3], and the magicians asked for a reward, which Fir'awn promised, with nearness to him [c4]. They asked whether Musa would throw first; he told them to throw, and they bewitched the people and brought great magic [c5]. In another passage Musa told them to throw what they were going to throw; they threw their ropes and staffs and said that by the might of Fir'awn they were the victors [c14]. Their ropes and staffs seemed to move and Musa felt fear within himself; God told him not to fear, that he was uppermost, and to throw what was in his right hand [c6]. His staff swallowed what they had fabricated, the truth was established and they were defeated [c7]. Another passage gives Musa's words after they threw: that God will make it vain and establishes the truth by His words [c8].

The magicians were cast down in prostration, saying “We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun” [c9]. Fir'awn said they had believed before his permission, that Musa was their chief who taught them magic, and that he would cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify them [c10]. They answered that there was no harm, that they would return to their Lord and hoped for forgiveness [c11], and in another passage that they would not prefer him over the clear proofs and over Him who created them [c12].

### Deep study

The day of the magicians is told in more than one passage, with a parallel structure [c1][c5][c9]. One has the scene-setting by Fir'awn and Musa [c1][c2] and Musa's fear [c6]. Others have the reward and the dialogue of the magicians [c4][c5] and the swallowing [c7]. The words of the magicians after their prostration are given in forms that agree on the Lord of the worlds [c9], with fuller responses in some [c11] and the declaration against the threat in another [c12]. The gathering of the plan in 20:64 [c13] and the cry by the might of Fir'awn in 26:44 [c14] are each in one passage only.

### Kids mode

Fir'awn set a day to meet Musa with his magicians [c1]. They threw their ropes and sticks, and it seemed to Musa that they were moving [c6]. God told him not to fear and to throw his staff [c6]. His staff swallowed what the magicians had made, and the magicians fell down and said they believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun [c7][c9]. The magicians threw their ropes and sticks and called on the might of Fir'awn [c14].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the magicians were the experts of their craft, and they recognised what they saw as different from their own work [c7][c9]. They then held to their belief when threatened [c11][c12].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: how many magicians there were, the place and date of the festival, the nature of their ropes and staffs beyond that they seemed to move, and whether the descriptions of the throwing describe separate moments. The fate of the magicians after the threat is not narrated. Who is meant by they in 20:62-64 is not marked in the ayat; the reading and grammar of 20:63 (a pair of magicians) are discussed by scholars.

## 10. The years of pressure  (`#the-years-of-pressure`)

>

>

>

### Claims

**c1** (7:127): The chiefs asked Fir'awn “Will you leave Musa and his people to spread corruption in the land and leave you and your gods?” he said “We will kill their sons and keep their women alive, and we are dominant over them.”

**c2** (7:128): Musa said to his people “Seek help in God and be patient; the earth is God's; he gives it as an inheritance to whom He wills of His servants; and the end is for the mindful.”

**c3** (7:129): They said “We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us.” he said “Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and then see how you act.”

**c4** (7:130-131): God seized the people of Fir'awn with years of drought and a shortage of fruits, so that they might remember; when good came they said it was theirs, and when evil struck they blamed Musa and those with him as an omen; God says their omen is with Him.

**c5** (7:132): They said “Whatever sign you bring to bewitch us with, we will not believe you.”

**c6** (7:133): God sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as detailed signs; they were arrogant and a criminal people.

**c7** (7:134-135): When the plague fell on them they said “Musa, call upon your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you; if you remove the plague from us, we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you”; when God removed it for a term which they were to reach, they broke their word.

**c8** (10:83): None believed Musa except some of the offspring (dhurriyyah) of his people, in fear that Fir'awn and his chiefs would persecute them; Fir'awn was high in the land and among the transgressors.

**c9** (10:84-86): Musa said “My people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims”; they said “In God we put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, and save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.”

**c10** (10:87): God inspired Musa and his brother to settle their people in houses in Misr, to make their houses a qiblah (the Arabic word qiblah is left untranslated here), to establish prayer, and to give good news to the believers.

**c11** (10:88-89): Musa said “Our Lord, You gave Fir'awn and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world; our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way; our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment.” God said “Your supplication has been answered, so be upright and do not follow the way of those who do not know.”

### One-minute summary

Fir'awn's chiefs urged him against Musa and his people, and he said he would kill their sons [c1]. Musa told his people to seek God's help and be patient [c2]. A drought and a shortage of fruits [c4] and the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood [c6] came on Fir'awn's people. They promised to believe if relieved and broke their word [c7]. Only some of the offspring of his people believed, in fear [c8]; Musa and his brother were told to settle their people in houses and establish prayer [c10].

### Complete story

The chiefs asked Fir'awn if he would leave Musa and his people to spread corruption and abandon him and his gods, and he said he would kill their sons and keep their women alive [c1]. Musa told his people to seek help in God and be patient, because the earth is God's and He gives it to whom He wills [c2]. They said they had been harmed before and after he came; he said that perhaps their Lord would destroy their enemy and make them successors, and see how they would act [c3].

God seized Fir'awn's people with years of drought and shortage of fruit so that they would remember; they credited good to themselves and blamed Musa and those with him for evil, and God says their omen is with Him [c4]. They said no sign would make them believe [c5]. God sent the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as detailed signs, and they were arrogant [c6]. When the plague fell they asked Musa to call upon his Lord, promising to believe and to send the Children of Israel; when it was removed they broke their word [c7].

Another passage says none believed Musa except some of the offspring (dhurriyyah) of his people, for fear of Fir'awn [c8]. Musa told them to rely upon God, and they said they trusted in God and asked not to be a trial for the wrongdoers and to be saved [c9]. God inspired Musa and his brother to settle their people in houses in Misr, to establish prayer and to give good news to the believers [c10]. Musa prayed about Fir'awn's adornment and wealth, and God said his supplication had been answered and told them to be upright [c11].

### Deep study

One passage records the pressure and the signs [c1][c4][c6][c7]; another records the limited number of believers and their prayers [c8][c9][c11]. The signs listed in the first are not claimed to be those mentioned elsewhere [c6]. The Arabic word dhurriyyah in [c8], offspring or descendants, is understood in more than one way by interpreters.

### Kids mode

Fir'awn's chiefs urged him against Musa and his people [c1]. Musa told them to ask God for help and to be patient [c2]. God sent signs to Fir'awn's people so that they would remember [c4][c6]. They promised to believe if the trouble stopped, but when it stopped they did not keep their word [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the account shows a promise made in hardship and broken in ease [c7]. It also shows a small group asking God for protection and trust in Him [c9].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the order, length and number of the plagues beyond those named in 7:133; how many believed; who the dhurriyyah were, since the ayat say offspring of his people; and the meaning of making houses a qiblah in 10:87, where interpreters differ.

### Claims

**c1** (26:52, 44:23): God inspired Musa and told him “Travel by night with My servants; you will be pursued.”

**c2** (26:53-56): Fir'awn sent gatherers into the cities, and said “These are a small band; they enrage us; and we are all on guard.”

**c3** (26:57-59): God took the people of Fir'awn out of gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station, and gave it as an inheritance to the Children of Israel.

**c4** (26:60-62): They pursued them at sunrise; when the pair of hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said “We are about to be overtaken”; he said “No; my Lord is with me; he will guide me.”

**c5** (26:63): God inspired Musa and said “Strike the sea with your staff”; it split, and each part was like a great mountain.

**c6** (20:77-78): In another passage, God told him to strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing neither being overtaken nor any other danger; Fir'awn followed them with his soldiers and the sea covered them with what covered them.

**c7** (26:64-67): God brought the others near, saved Musa and all who were with him, and then drowned the others; in that is a sign, and most of them were not believers.

**c8** (2:50): God says that He parted the sea for them and saved them and drowned the family of Fir'awn while they were watching.

**c9** (10:90): God says that He took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Fir'awn and his soldiers followed in transgression and enmity; when drowning overtook him he said “I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.”

**c10** (10:91-92): He was told “Now? While you disobeyed before and were among the corrupters? Today We will save you in your body, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you; many people are heedless of Our signs.”

**c12** (28:39-42): Fir'awn and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right and thought they would not be returned to God; God seized him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea, made them leaders calling to the Fire, followed them with a curse in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.

**c13** (17:103): Fir'awn wished to drive them from the land, and God drowned him and those with him all together.

**c11** (44:24, 44:30-31): Another passage says that Musa was told to leave the sea calm (the word rendered calm, rahwan, is read in more than one way), for they were a host to be drowned; and that God saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment, from Fir'awn, who was high and among the transgressors.

**c14** (20:79): Fir'awn led his people astray and did not guide them.

**c15** (26:68): The ayah after the sign says: indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.

**c16** (44:25-29): That passage also says how many gardens and springs, crops and a noble station they left, and the comfort in which they took pleasure; that God gave it as an inheritance to another people; and that neither the sky nor the earth wept over them, and they were not given respite.

### One-minute summary

Musa was told to travel by night with God's servants and that they would be pursued [c1]. Fir'awn sent gatherers [c2]. At the sea, Musa said his Lord was with him [c4] and was told to strike it; it split [c5][c6]. Musa and those with him were saved and Fir'awn's host was drowned [c7][c8][c9]. Another passage says that God saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment [c11], and that those drowned left gardens and springs behind [c16].

### Complete story

God inspired Musa to travel by night with His servants and told him they would be pursued [c1]. Fir'awn sent gatherers into the cities, calling Musa's people a small band who enraged him [c2]. God says He took the people of Fir'awn out of gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station and gave it as an inheritance to the Children of Israel [c3].

They pursued at sunrise; when the pair of hosts saw each other, Musa's companions said they were about to be overtaken, and Musa said his Lord was with him and would guide him [c4]. God told him to strike the sea with his staff, and it split, each part like a great mountain [c5]. Another passage says to strike a dry path in the sea, with no fear of being overtaken, and that the sea covered Fir'awn and his soldiers [c6]. It also says that Fir'awn led his people astray and did not guide them [c14]. God brought the others near, saved Musa and all with him, and drowned the others [c7]. The ayah after the sign says that your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful [c15]. Another passage says God parted the sea and drowned the family of Fir'awn while the Children of Israel were watching [c8].

When drowning overtook Fir'awn, he said he believed that there is no god but the One in whom the Children of Israel believe; he was answered with “Now”? and told he would be saved in his body as a sign for those after him [c9][c10]. Another passage says God cast Fir'awn and his soldiers into the sea [c12]. Another passage says Fir'awn wished to drive them from the land and God drowned him and those with him together [c13].

Another passage says that Musa was told to leave the sea calm, for they were a host to be drowned, and that God saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment, from Fir'awn, who was high and among the transgressors [c11]. It says how many gardens, springs, crops and a noble station they left, and the comfort in which they took pleasure, that God gave it as an inheritance to another people, and that neither the sky nor the earth wept over them and they were not given respite [c16].

### Deep study

One passage gives the fullest sequence: the command, the pursuit, the fear, the sea, the rescue and the drowning [c1][c4][c5][c7]. Another says a dry path [c6]. The words saved in your body in 10:92 are stated in the text without explanation [c10]. The exchange with the drowning Fir'awn is in one passage only [c9][c10]. The ayat that name the inheritance of gardens and springs do not say it was the land spoken of in other chapters [c3]. The call to leave the sea calm [c11] and the list of what the drowned left behind [c16] are in the passage on the humiliating punishment only. The ayah that says another people inherited it [c16] does not name them, while the earlier passage names the Children of Israel as the heirs [c3].

### Kids mode

God told Musa to leave at night with his people [c1]. When Musa's people saw the army and the sea, they were afraid, but Musa said his Lord was with him [c4]. God told Musa to strike the sea with his staff, and it split [c5]. Musa and his people were saved [c7]. God saved the Children of Israel from Fir'awn [c11].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the group's fear at the sea is answered by one sentence, “my Lord is with me; He will guide me” [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the name or the place of the sea, which the ayat call bahr and yamm; the date; the number of people who crossed; the place on the far shore; and what God did with the body of Fir'awn beyond saving it as a sign. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of a body with a named king. The land inherited in 26:59 is not named. The word rahwan in 44:24 is read in more than one way (calm, open or parted); the draft leaves it open.
