>
> **5:26** قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً يَتِيهُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَلَا تَأْسَ عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:57, 7:160, 20:80-81): God says He shaded them with the cloud and sent down upon them al-mann and as-salwa (rendered here manna and salwa), telling them to eat of the good things He provided; they did not wrong Him, but they wronged themselves.

**c2** (2:60, 7:160): When Musa asked for water for his people, God told him to strike the stone with his staff, and springs gushed from it, one for each people; each people knew its drinking place; they were told to eat and drink of God's provision and not to spread corruption in the land.

**c3** (7:160): God divided them into tribes, as nations.

**c4** (2:61): They said “Musa, we cannot endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to bring forth for us of what the earth grows, its herbs, cucumbers, fum, lentils and onions” (fum is rendered by interpreters as garlic or as wheat); he said “Would you exchange what is better for what is lower? Go down to a town (misran), for you will have what you asked.”

**c5** (2:58-59, 7:161-162): They were told to enter a town, eat from it wherever they wished, enter the gate prostrating, and say “Hittah” so that God would forgive their mistakes; those who did wrong changed the word they had been given, and God sent a punishment (rijz) from the heaven on them.

**c6** (20:80-82): In another passage, God recalls to the Children of Israel that He saved them from their enemy, promised them the right side of the mountain, and sent down the manna and the salwa; he warns them not to transgress in it, for His anger would descend; and says He is Forgiving to the one who repents, believes and does good and then is guided.

**c7** (5:20-21): Musa reminded his people of God's favour, that He placed prophets among them, made them kings and gave them what He had not given anyone in the worlds, and told them to enter the holy land which God had assigned to them and not to turn back.

**c8** (5:22-23): They said “Musa, there is a people of tyrants in it, and we will not enter until they leave; if they leave, we will enter”; a pair of men of those who feared, whom God had favoured, said “Enter upon them by the gate; when you enter it, you will be the victors; and rely upon God, if you are believers.”

**c9** (5:24): They said “Musa, we will never enter it as long as they are in it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are sitting here.”

**c10** (5:25-26): Musa said “My Lord, I have power over none but myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiantly disobedient people.” God said the land would be forbidden to them for years, during which they would wander in the earth, and told Musa not to grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.

### One-minute summary

In the wilderness the Children of Israel were shaded and given manna and salwa [c1] and water from a stone [c2]. They asked for other foods [c4]. When told to enter the holy land they refused [c8][c9], and Musa asked to be separated from them; God said the land would be forbidden for years [c10].

### Complete story

God says He shaded them with the cloud and sent down the manna and the salwa, telling them to eat of the good things [c1]. When Musa asked for water for his people, he was told to strike the stone with his staff, and springs gushed forth, one for each people, each people knowing its drinking place [c2]; they were divided into tribes [c3]. They then said they could not endure one kind of food, and asked for herbs, cucumbers, fum, lentils and onions; Musa asked if they would exchange better for lower [c4]. They were told to enter a town, eat freely, enter the gate prostrating and say “Hittah”; those who did wrong changed the word and a punishment was sent from the heaven [c5]. Another passage recalls the favours and warns against transgression, while saying that God forgives the one who repents [c6].

Another passage records Musa's reminder of the favours, and the command to enter the holy land [c7]. His people said there were tyrants and that they would not enter until they left; a pair of men whom God had favoured said to enter by the gate and rely on God [c8]. His people answered that they would never enter and that Musa and his Lord should go and fight while they sat [c9]. Musa said he had power only over himself and his brother and asked to be separated from them; God said the land was forbidden to them for years while they wandered [c10].

### Deep study

Provision (manna, salwa, shade, water) [c1][c2] and refusal (the foods [c4], the gate [c5], the land [c8][c9]) are interwoven in these passages without a fixed order. The word misran in [c4] can be read as a town or as the name Misr; it is flagged for review. The decree of years of wandering [c10] follows Musa's own words that he has power only over himself and his brother [c10]. The town of [c5] and the holy land of [c7] are not stated to be the same place.

### Kids mode

God told Musa to strike a stone, and springs came out of it [c1][c2]. Later Musa told his people to enter the holy land, but they said they would not enter until the people in it left, and that they would sit where they were [c8][c9].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the account sets God's provision [c1][c2] beside the people's complaints [c4] and refusals [c9]. A pair of men who feared still urged trust in God [c8].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the place of the wandering, the identity of the ‘a pair of men’ in 5:23 (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text; none is used here), the names of the tribes, the identity of the ‘town’ and the ‘holy land’ (the ayat do not name them), how the ‘punishment from the heaven’ of 2:59 took place, and whether the years began at once.

> **20:83** وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
>
> **20:84** قَالَ هُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ

### Claims

**c1** (7:142): God appointed thirty nights for Musa and completed them with ten, so that the appointed time of his Lord was completed; Musa said to his brother Harun “Take my place among my people, set things right, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.”

**c2** (20:83-84): In another passage, God asked “What made you hasten from your people, Musa?” and he said “They are on my track, and I hastened to You, my Lord, so that You would be pleased.”

**c3** (7:143): When Musa came at the appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said “My Lord, show me, that I may look at You.” God said “You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it stays in its place, then you will see Me.”

**c4** (7:143): When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell unconscious; when he recovered he said “Glory be to You; I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers.”

**c5** (7:144): God said “Musa, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My speech; so take what I have given you and be among the grateful.”

**c6** (7:145): God wrote for him in the tablets (al-alwah) of everything, an admonition and a detailing of everything, and told him to take them with strength and command his people to take the best of them.

**c7** (7:146-147): God says He will turn away from His signs those who are arrogant in the land without right, so that even if they see every sign they do not believe, and that those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds are worthless.

**c8** (2:53): God says that He gave Musa the Book and the Criterion (al-furqan) so that they might be guided.

**c9** (7:154): When Musa's anger subsided he took up the tablets, and in what was written in them was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord.

**c10** (7:155): Musa chose seventy men of his people for God's appointment; when the quake seized them he said “My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us did? It is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will; You are our protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us.”

**c11** (7:156): Musa asked for good in this world and the Hereafter, and said “we have turned to You”; God said His punishment strikes whom He wills, and His mercy encompasses all things, and He will write it down for those who are mindful, give zakat and believe in His signs.

### One-minute summary

God appointed nights for Musa, and he left Harun in charge of his people [c1]. Musa asked to look at his Lord, and the mountain crumbled [c3][c4]. God told him He had chosen him with His messages and speech [c5], and wrote the tablets for him [c6]. Musa also chose seventy men for the appointment [c10].

### Complete story

God appointed thirty nights for Musa and completed them with ten, so that the appointed time was completed; Musa told Harun to take his place and set things right [c1]. In another passage God asked what made him hasten from his people, and he said he hastened so that God would be pleased [c2]. When he came at the appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he asked to look at God; God said he would not see Him, but to look at the mountain [c3]. When God manifested to the mountain it crumbled and Musa fell unconscious; when he recovered he said “Glory be to You; I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers” [c4]. God said He had chosen him over the people with His messages and speech and told him to take what He gave and be grateful [c5]. He wrote for Musa in the tablets of everything, an admonition and a detailing, and told him to take them with strength and command his people to take the best of them [c6]. Another passage says God gave Musa the Book and the Criterion [c8]. God also says He will turn the arrogant away from His signs [c7].

After his anger subsided he took up the tablets; in their writing was guidance and mercy [c9]. Musa chose seventy men for the appointment, and when the quake seized them he prayed for forgiveness and mercy [c10]. God answered that His mercy encompassed all things and would be written down for those who are mindful [c11].

### Deep study

The meeting is told as an appointed time with a stated length [c1], a request [c3], an event on the mountain [c4], and a reply that names what God gave: the messages, the speech and the tablets [c5][c6]. The word furqan, rendered Criterion, is a topic for scholarly review [c8]. The text gives no statement that the seventy men were chosen after the calf, and this draft claims no order [c10].

### Kids mode

God appointed nights for Musa to meet Him [c1]. Musa left his brother Harun to look after the people [c1]. God spoke to Musa and gave him tablets with guidance written in them [c5][c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Musa asks for something and is told what he cannot have, with a sign given instead [c3][c4]. He then responds with repentance and the first words of faith [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: what the tablets were made of, what was written in them beyond the general description, where the appointment was, who the seventy men were, and whether the thirty and ten nights were separate stages. The ayat say only that God manifested Himself to the mountain; this draft gives no further description. Whether the quake of 7:155 and the thunderbolt of 2:55 are the same event is a question for scholars.

### Claims

**c1** (7:138-140): After God took the Children of Israel across the sea, they came upon a people devoted to idols of theirs and said “Musa, make for us a god as they have gods”; he said “You are a people who are ignorant”, and “Shall I seek for you any god other than God, when He has favoured you over the worlds?”

**c2** (20:85): God told Musa “We have tried your people after you, and the Samiri has led them astray.”

**c3** (20:86): Musa returned to his people angry and grieved and said “My people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise? Did the covenant seem long to you, or did you want anger from your Lord to descend on you, so you broke your promise to me?”

**c4** (20:87-88): They said “We did not break our promise to you of our own will, but we were made to carry loads of the people's ornaments, so we threw them, and so did the Samiri cast”; he brought out for them a calf, a body that had a lowing, and they said “This is your god and the god of Musa.” (The next word, fa-nasiya, has its subject read differently by interpreters and is not translated here.)

**c5** (20:89, 7:148): God says that they did not see that it returned no word to them and had no power to harm or benefit them; and that people of Musa took, after he left, a calf from their ornaments, a body having a lowing, and it neither spoke to them nor guided them to a way.

**c6** (20:90-91): Harun had said to them before “My people, you are only being tried with it; your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order”; they said “We will not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returns to us.”

**c7** (20:92-94): Musa asked Harun “What prevented you, when you saw them go astray, from following me? Did you disobey my order?” Harun, addressing him as son of his mother, asked not to be seized, and said he had feared that Musa would say he had caused division among the Children of Israel and had not observed his word.

**c8** (7:150): In another passage, Musa returned angry and grieved, said “What an evil thing you did in my place after me! Did you hasten the command of your Lord?”, threw down the tablets and seized his brother's head, pulling him toward him; Harun said “Son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies rejoice at me and do not put me with the wrongdoing people.”

**c9** (7:151): Musa said “My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy; You are the most merciful of the merciful.”

**c10** (20:95-97): Musa asked the Samiri “What is your case, Samiri?” he said “I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus my soul suggested to me.” Musa said “Go; in this life it is for you to say ‘no touching’; and you have an appointment you will not miss; look at your god to which you were devoted; we will burn it and scatter it in the sea.”

**c11** (20:98): Musa said “Your God is only God, other than whom there is no god; he has encompassed all things in knowledge.”

**c12** (7:149): When they regretted and saw that they had gone astray, they said “If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.”

**c13** (7:152-153): God says those who took the calf will be struck by anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world, while your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful to those who did evil, then repented and believed.

**c14** (2:51-52): In another passage, God says that He appointed nights for Musa and then they took the calf after he left, being wrongdoers; then He pardoned them after that so that they might be thankful.

**c15** (2:54): Musa said to his people “My people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf, so repent to your Maker and kill yourselves (fa-qtulu anfusakum); that is better for you with your Maker”; and He accepted their repentance.

**c16** (7:141): The passage goes on: and when We saved you from the people of Fir'awn, who afflicted you with the worst torment, killing your sons and keeping your women alive; in that was a great trial from your Lord. (The ayah does not mark who speaks.)

### One-minute summary

After the crossing the Children of Israel asked Musa for a god like those of a people devoted to idols [c1]. The passage goes on to recall their rescue from the people of Fir'awn [c16]. While Musa was away, the Samiri brought out a calf, and they took it [c2][c4][c5]. Musa returned angry [c3][c8], questioned Harun [c7][c8], and the Samiri [c10]. The people repented [c12]; God says He pardoned them [c14].

### Complete story

After the crossing the people came upon others devoted to idols and asked Musa to make them a god; he said they were ignorant and asked whether he should seek a god other than God [c1]. The passage goes on to recall the rescue from the people of Fir'awn, who afflicted them with the worst torment, killing their sons and keeping their women alive, and calls this a great trial from their Lord [c16]. While Musa was away, God told him that his people had been tried and that the Samiri had led them astray [c2]. Musa returned angry and grieved and asked whether the covenant had seemed long to them [c3]. They said they were made to carry loads of the people's ornaments, threw them, and that the Samiri cast too; he brought out a calf, a body with a lowing, and they said “This is your god and the god of Musa” [c4]. God says it returned no word and had no power to harm or benefit [c5]. Harun had said they were being tried by it and to follow him; they said they would keep to it until Musa returned [c6].

Musa asked Harun what had prevented him, and Harun asked not to be seized and spoke of his fear of causing division [c7]. Another passage records Musa throwing down the tablets and seizing his brother's head, and Harun's answer that the people deemed him weak and nearly killed him [c8]. Musa prayed for forgiveness for himself and his brother [c9]. He asked the Samiri what his case was; the Samiri said he took a handful from the track of the messenger and threw it, as his soul suggested [c10]. Musa told him that his god would be burned and scattered in the sea [c10], and said that their God is only God [c11].

The people, when they regretted, asked for mercy and forgiveness [c12]. God says those who took the calf would be struck by anger and humiliation, and that He is Forgiving to those who repent [c13]. Another passage says God pardoned them after the appointed nights [c14], and records Musa telling them to repent to their Maker and kill themselves, and that He accepted their repentance [c15].

### Deep study

The calf is told in more than one passage [c4][c5][c8]. The longest sequence has God's information to Musa [c2], the people's explanation [c4], Harun's earlier warning [c6], and Musa's exchanges with Harun [c7] and the Samiri [c10]. A shorter account has Musa's reaction in physical terms and Harun's answer in different words, that the people deemed him weak [c8]. Both answers of Harun are stated in the text and are not set against one another in this draft [c7][c8]. Another places the calf after the appointed nights and records the instruction to kill yourselves [c14][c15]. The ayah that follows Musa's words recalls the rescue from Fir'awn's people and calls it a great trial [c16]; it does not say who speaks.

### Kids mode

The Samiri made a calf, and the people took it [c4][c5]. Harun told them it was a test and that their Lord is the Most Merciful [c6]. Musa said that their God is only God [c11]. The people were sorry and asked God for mercy [c12].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the account shows a community being led away in a leader's absence [c4], a brother who warned them [c6], and the opening of repentance afterwards [c12][c14].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: what the calf was made of beyond ‘a body having a lowing’ (the ayat say it was made of the people's ornaments), the Samiri's origin, what ‘a handful from the track of the messenger’ refers to (interpreters differ; Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of the ‘messenger’ and the ‘track’), how the repentance of 2:54 was carried out, and the number of those who took the calf. The speaker of 7:141 is not marked: it may continue Musa's words or be spoken by God, and the draft does not choose.

## 15. The covenant and the mountain  (`#the-covenant-and-the-mountain`)

Cited ayat: 2:63, 2:93, 4:154, 7:171

> **2:63** وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ

> **2:93** وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱسْمَعُوا۟ قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَأُشْرِبُوا۟ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِيمَٰنُكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

> **4:154** وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ ٱلطُّورَ بِمِيثَٰقِهِمْ وَقُلْنَا لَهُمُ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ لَا تَعْدُوا۟ فِى ٱلسَّبْتِ وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظًا

> **7:171** وَإِذْ نَتَقْنَا ٱلْجَبَلَ فَوْقَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُۥ ظُلَّةٌ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُۥ وَاقِعٌۢ بِهِمْ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:63): God says He took their covenant and raised the mountain (at-Tur) above them, and said “Take what We have given you with strength and remember what is in it, so that you may be mindful.”

**c2** (7:171): Another passage says He lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy and they thought it was going to fall on them, and told them to take what He gave them with strength and remember what is in it.

**c3** (2:93): A later ayah repeats the reminder of the covenant and the mountain, and says they said “We hear and we disobey”; and that the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their disbelief.

**c4** (4:154): A further passage says God raised the mountain above them with their covenant, and told them to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and took from them a solemn covenant.

### One-minute summary

These ayat recall a covenant taken from a people with the mountain raised above them [c1][c2][c4]. They were told to take what they had been given with strength and to remember what is in it [c1][c2]. One recalls that they said “We hear and we disobey” [c3].

### Complete story

God says He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it [c1]. Another passage describes the mountain lifted above them as if it were a canopy, so that they thought it would fall on them [c2]. A later ayah repeats the reminder, adds that they said “We hear and we disobey”, and that the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of disbelief [c3]. A further passage mentions the raising of the mountain with their covenant, the command to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and a solemn covenant [c4].

### Deep study

The ayat do not say where the covenant fits in the order of the other events in this account [c1][c2][c3][c4]. The phrase take what We have given you with strength is in more than one ayah [c1][c2]. The ayah that repeats the reminder ties the covenant to their reply and to the calf [c3]. The last passage lists the content of the covenant as the gate, prostration and the Sabbath [c4]; the ayat do not say that this gate is the gate spoken of in the chapter on provision and the wilderness [c4].

### Kids mode

God took a promise from the people and told them to hold on to what He gave them with strength and remember what is in it [c1][c2]. They said “We hear and we disobey” [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): hearing a command is different from obeying it, and the ayah sets hearing and disobeying side by side in the people's own words [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established in the ayat: when this took place in relation to the tablets or the calf, the nature of the raising of the mountain (interpreters differ on whether it is literal), and what the gate and the Sabbath refer to in 4:154.
- Who is addressed is read from the surrounding passages; these ayat say you and them and do not name the people.
- The relation between 2:63 and 2:93, a repeated reminder in the same surah, is a matter for scholars.

>
> **18:82** وَأَمَّا ٱلْجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَٰمَيْنِ يَتِيمَيْنِ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحْتَهُۥ كَنزٌ لَّهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَٰلِحًا فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَن يَبْلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا وَيَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُۥ عَنْ أَمْرِى ذَٰلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًا

### Claims

**c1** (18:60): Musa said to his young man “I will not cease until I reach the meeting of the pair seas, or I will go on for a long time.”

**c2** (18:61-64): When they reached the meeting of the pair, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the sea; after they passed on, Musa asked for their meal, saying they had met with fatigue on the journey; the young man said he had forgotten the fish at the rock and only Satan made him forget to mention it; Musa said “That is what we were seeking”, and they went back retracing their steps.

**c3** (18:65): They found a servant from among God's servants, to whom He had given mercy from Himself and taught knowledge from Himself.

**c4** (18:66-68): Musa asked “May I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance?” he said “You will never be able to be patient with me; and how can you be patient about what you have not encompassed in knowledge?”

**c5** (18:69-70): Musa said “You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order”; he said “If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you.”

**c6** (18:71-73): When they boarded the boat he made a hole in it; Musa said “Did you make a hole in it to drown its people? You have done a grave thing.” he said “Did I not say that you would never be able to be patient with me?” Musa said “Do not hold me to account for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.”

**c7** (18:74-76): They met a boy and he killed him; Musa said “Have you killed a pure soul, not for a soul? You have done a terrible thing.” he repeated his earlier question, and Musa said “If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me as a companion; you have received an excuse from me.”

**c8** (18:77): They came to the people of a town and asked for food, and the people refused to host them; they found in it a wall about to fall, and he set it straight; Musa said “If you wished, you could have taken a payment for it.”

**c9** (18:78): He said “This is the parting between me and you; I will inform you of the interpretation of what you were not able to be patient about.”

**c10** (18:79): The boat belonged to poor people working at sea; he wished to damage it because behind them was a king seizing every boat by force.

**c11** (18:80-81): The servant said the boy's parents were believers and “we feared” that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief, so “we wished” that their Lord would give them in exchange one better than him in purity and nearer in mercy.

**c12** (18:82): The wall belonged to a pair of orphan boys in the town, and beneath it was a treasure for them; their father was righteous, and your Lord wished that they reach their maturity and take out their treasure as a mercy from your Lord; “I did not do it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of what you were not able to be patient about.”

### One-minute summary

Musa set out with his young man to the meeting of the seas [c1] and lost their fish [c2]. They found a servant given mercy and knowledge [c3]. Musa asked to follow him and was warned he would not be able to be patient [c4]. What the servant did puzzled Musa [c6][c7][c8]; the servant then gave the interpretation of each [c10][c11][c12].

### Complete story

Musa told his young man he would not cease until reaching the meeting of the pair seas [c1]. They forgot the fish there, and it went into the sea; when they stopped for their meal, the young man said he had forgotten it, and Musa said that was what they were seeking, and they went back [c2]. They found a servant from among God's servants, given mercy and knowledge from God [c3]. Musa asked to follow him to be taught, and the servant said he would not be able to be patient with what he had not encompassed in knowledge [c4]. Musa said he would be patient and obedient; the servant told him not to ask about anything until he himself mentioned it [c5].

He made a hole in a boat; Musa objected and was reminded of the condition [c6]. He killed a boy; Musa objected again and said that if he asked again the servant should not keep him as a companion [c7]. In a town that had refused them hospitality, he set a wall straight, and Musa said he could have taken payment [c8]. He said it was the parting and he would give the interpretation [c9].

The boat belonged to poor people, and a king seized every boat by force [c10]. The servant said the boy's parents were believers and “we feared” he would burden them with transgression and disbelief, so “we wished” for one better in exchange [c11]. The wall belonged to a pair of orphans with a treasure beneath it, from a righteous father; their Lord wished them to reach maturity and take out the treasure, and the servant said he had not done it on his own accord [c12].

### Deep study

The passage has a framing of travel and a loss [c1][c2], a request and a condition [c4][c5], incidents each answered by Musa's objection [c6][c7][c8], and explanations [c10][c11][c12]. In the explanations the speaker moves between I wished [c10], we feared and we wished [c11], and your Lord wished [c12], and ends with a statement that he did not do it of his own accord [c12].

### Kids mode

Musa travelled to find a servant of God who had special knowledge [c3]. He asked to follow him and learn, and the servant said Musa would not be able to be patient [c4]. The servant did things that Musa did not understand [c6][c7][c8], and at the end the servant explained each one [c10][c11][c12].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the account is about the limits of what a person sees at one moment [c4], and it records that each act had a reason that could only be told afterwards [c10][c11][c12]. It also shows a prophet asking to learn from another [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

Not established in the ayat: the name of the servant (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: al-Khidr), the name of Musa's young man (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text), the place called the meeting of the seas, the identity of the king, the town, the boy and the orphans, and the kind of fish. The ayat say Musa and do not add a father's name; reading him as the Musa of the other chapters is the common reading. Whether the servant was a prophet is not stated; the ayat say he was given mercy and knowledge from God.

## 17. The messenger remembered  (`#the-messenger-remembered`)

Cited ayat: 14:5-8, 61:5, 37:114-122, 17:101-104

> **14:5** وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنْ أَخْرِجْ قَوْمَكَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ وَذَكِّرْهُم بِأَيَّىٰمِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ
>
> **14:6** وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنجَىٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ
>
> **14:7** وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ وَلَئِن كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِى لَشَدِيدٌ
>
> **14:8** وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِن تَكْفُرُوٓا۟ أَنتُمْ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَنِىٌّ حَمِيدٌ

> **61:5** وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ لِمَ تُؤْذُونَنِى وَقَد تَّعْلَمُونَ أَنِّى رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ فَلَمَّا زَاغُوٓا۟ أَزَاغَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ

> **37:114** وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
>
> **37:115** وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُمَا وَقَوْمَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
>
> **37:116** وَنَصَرْنَٰهُمْ فَكَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
>
> **37:117** وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُمَا ٱلْكِتَٰبَ ٱلْمُسْتَبِينَ
>
> **37:118** وَهَدَيْنَٰهُمَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ
>
> **37:119** وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِمَا فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ
>
> **37:120** سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
>
> **37:121** إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
>
> **37:122** إِنَّهُمَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

> **17:101** وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍ فَسْـَٔلْ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ فَقَالَ لَهُۥ فِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ مَسْحُورًا
>
> **17:102** قَالَ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ بَصَآئِرَ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ يَٰفِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا
>
> **17:103** فَأَرَادَ أَن يَسْتَفِزَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ جَمِيعًا
>
> **17:104** وَقُلْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ لِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱسْكُنُوا۟ ٱلْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ جِئْنَا بِكُمْ لَفِيفًا

### Claims

**c1** (14:5): God says He sent Musa with His signs: “Bring your people out from the darknesses to the light, and remind them of the days of God.”

**c2** (14:6): Musa said to his people “Remember God's favour upon you when He saved you from the family of Fir'awn, who inflicted on you the worst of torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive; in that was a great trial from your Lord.”

**c3** (14:7-8): God announced “If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, My punishment is severe”; and Musa said “If you are ungrateful, you and all those on earth, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy.”

**c4** (61:5): Musa said to his people “My people, why do you harm me when you know that I am the messenger of God to you?” and when they deviated, God let their hearts deviate.

**c5** (37:114-122): God says He bestowed favour on Musa and Harun, saved them and their people from the great distress, helped them so that they were the victors, gave them the clear Book, guided them to the straight path, left a good mention of them among later generations, and said “Peace be upon Musa and Harun”; they were among His believing servants.

**c6** (17:101-102): God says He gave Musa nine clear signs; Musa was told to ask the Children of Israel when he came to them; Fir'awn said “I think you, Musa, are bewitched”, and Musa said “You know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear proofs, and I think, Fir'awn, that you are doomed.”

**c7** (17:103-104): Fir'awn wished to drive them out of the land and God drowned him and those with him together; after him God said to the Children of Israel “Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you all together.”

### One-minute summary

Musa was sent to bring his people from the darknesses to the light and to remind them of God's days [c1][c2]. The ayat record his words on gratitude [c3] and on being harmed by his own people [c4], and God's praise and peace upon Musa and Harun [c5]. They also recall the nine signs and the end of Fir'awn [c6][c7].

### Complete story

God says He sent Musa with His signs to bring his people out from the darknesses to the light and remind them of the days of God [c1]. Musa told them to remember God's favour in saving them from the family of Fir'awn [c2]. God announced that gratitude brings increase and ingratitude a severe punishment, and Musa said that if all on earth were ungrateful, God is Free of need [c3]. Musa also asked his people why they harmed him when they knew he was the messenger of God to them; when they deviated, God let their hearts deviate [c4].

Another passage says God bestowed favour on Musa and Harun, saved them and their people, helped them, gave them the clear Book and the straight path, left a good mention of them and said “Peace be upon Musa and Harun” [c5]. Another passage says God gave Musa nine clear signs, and records Fir'awn calling him bewitched and Musa calling Fir'awn doomed [c6]. It adds that Fir'awn wished to drive them out of the land and was drowned, and the Children of Israel were told to dwell in the land [c7].

### Deep study

This closing chapter gathers statements about Musa that stand outside a single scene [c1][c4][c5]. His speech to his people is a reminder of favour and a statement on gratitude [c2][c3]. Another passage presents the same messenger from both sides: what he told his people [c1][c2][c3] and what God says of him and Harun [c5]. The nine clear signs are stated without a list [c6].

### Kids mode

God sent Musa to teach his people to remember God and to be thankful [c1][c3]. God says that He gave Musa and Harun the Book and guided them [c5]. God says “Peace be upon Musa and Harun” [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): the ayat state a principle in Musa's words, that gratitude brings increase [c3], and they record that a prophet can be harmed by his own people while his message stands [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

What the Quranic text does not state about Musa, as far as the ayat in this draft go: his death, burial or age; the name of his wife and children; the fate of Harun beyond the ayat cited; the dates of any event; the number of the Children of Israel; the list of the nine signs; and the fate of the believing magicians. The cow of the Children of Israel and other accounts are not covered in this draft. The scriptures that came earlier and the later traditions of the Children of Israel are outside this phase.
